biomes.name: Willow Meadow
biomes.tagline: A quiet grassland watched by fox and hawk
biomes.habitatNote: Deep grass on clay soil, hedgerows at the edge, one old oak.
rules: Grass is the only food that makes itself: it grows back toward what the soil can carry.
Every consumer eats, then births follow food — well-fed animals multiply, hungry ones starve.
Nothing here hunts foxes or hawks: their numbers are set by food alone.

species.label: Grass
notes: Grows logistically: the closer to capacity, the slower it grows.
Above capacity (after drought or a grazing spike) it dies back.

species.label: Rabbits
notes: Each rabbit harvests a small share of the standing grass every season.
Rabbit births scale with how well the herd was fed; scarce grass means starvation.

species.label: Foxes
notes: Foxes eat rabbits; a fox family needs a dense rabbit population to stay fed.
When rabbits crash, foxes starve the next season — watch the lag.

species.label: Hawks
notes: Hawks hunt the same rabbits as foxes — two hunters share one meal.
Wide wings need open sky: hawks only multiply when rabbits are plentiful.

biomes.name: Heron Wetland
biomes.tagline: A slow marsh where everything begins with reeds
biomes.habitatNote: Shallow water, reed islands, warmer air than the meadow.
rules: Reeds are the engine: every other species traces back to them in one or two steps.
Frogs sit in the middle — eaten by herons, fed by hoppers.
A long food chain amplifies mistakes: small changes at the bottom arrive big at the top.

species.label: Reeds
notes: Grows back toward the marsh's carrying capacity each season.
Reed beds shrink for good when habitat is drained — capacity, not just stems, is lost.

species.label: Hoppers
notes: Hoppers (marsh grasshoppers) graze reeds and multiply fast when fed.
They are the bridge species: almost everything above them depends on their numbers.

species.label: Frogs
notes: Frogs eat hoppers; a frog needs a thick cloud of hoppers to breed.
Frogs respond one season after hoppers move — count the lag in the chart.

species.label: Herons
notes: Herons spear frogs in the shallows; they need the deepest frog population of any hunter.
Lose the frogs and the herons stand empty-beaked — then leave.
